title: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) & IoT Security

sections.section: Section 5: OT/IoT Threat and Vulnerability Overview
sections.content: Operational Technology and IoT devices are vulnerable to volumetric network denial-of-service (DDoS/DoS) attacks, unauthorized command injection, ARP spoofing, and rogue gateway masquerading. Constrained IoT microcontrollers lack cryptographic hardware acceleration, making them prone to resource exhaustion when bombarded with high-rate packet floods.

IoT field devices, sensors, and actuators must be segregated into dedicated security zones (Purdue Level 1/0) using firewalls, VLANs, and micro-segmentation. Cross-zone communication must be strictly restricted to stateful inspection proxies to isolate lateral movement.

Defensive automated response mechanisms on safety-critical IoT (e.g., medical infusion devices, industrial programmable logic controllers) must prioritize non-destructive isolation (quarantine VLAN) over abrupt port shutdown. Automated mitigations must provide transparent explainability and enforce human-in-the-loop analyst authorization before persistent configuration changes.

sections.section: Section 6.7: Detection Signatures & Flow Rate Anomaly Monitoring
sections.content: Network flow anomalies such as rapid deviations in packet rate (Rate > 1000 pkts/s), source burst rate (Srate), destination drift (Drate), and irregular TCP flags (excessive SYN without ACK or unexpected RST/FIN counts) are primary indicators of ongoing denial of service or network reconnaissance.
